clue.text: Signs agreement enclosing minute area for itinerants

indicators.note: the nodding word wraps round the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: someone who signs agreement with a movement of the head nods

explanation.surface: Someone signs a contract that includes a tiny plot of land, all for the benefit of travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerants are people who travel from place to place with no settled home, a close synonym.

clue.text: In that way, Asian islander upset Indians

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the combined pieces upside down, so they read from the bottom

parts.note: so means in that way, as in do it so
a Javan is a native of Java in Indonesia

explanation.surface: An Asian islander is upset with some native Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Navajo are a Native American people of the south-west, the 'Indians' of older usage.

clue.text: After short time, lines put over end of dinghy producing fish

indicators.note: the line letters come after the brief time
in a down clue, over places a piece above the next one

parts.note: mo, short for moment, is a short time

indicators.note: the last letter of dinghy is taken

explanation.surface: Shortly afterwards, fishing lines are cast from the back of a small boat to catch something.
explanation.definitionFit: A molly is a small tropical freshwater fish kept in aquariums, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Innovative resident introducing new service for consumers

indicators.note: the rearranged resident takes in the letter for new
an innovative approach makes the letters of resident new, rearranging them

explanation.surface: An enterprising local launches a fresh service for customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innovative' rearranges RESIDENT to DINERSET, and 'introducing' puts N inside it after DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A service here is a matching set of crockery, and the consumers are diners eating their meal from it.

clue.text: Terribly mistreated, without one right or freedom

indicators.note: letters that are mistreated are knocked about into a new order
one copy of the letter for right is left out of the fodder before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone badly abused, stripped of a right or their freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRIBLY has two Rs; 'without one right' drops one, and 'mistreated' rearranges the remaining TERIBLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberty and freedom are plain synonyms for the state of not being restrained.

clue.text: Liberal American writer upset former European monarch

indicators.note: in a down clue the writer's name is turned upside down

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was the American writer of tales of horror
old means former, as in an old flame

explanation.surface: A liberal American author upset an ex-king in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'former' does double duty in sense only: it gives OLD while the definition is a monarch of the past, such as Leopold of Belgium. Leopold is also Bloom's first name in Joyce's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Leopold I and II were kings of the Belgians, so a European monarch of the past is a definition by example.

clue.text: Finishes off big job you pronounced a gem

indicators.note: the endings of the two words big and job are taken off

parts.note: the two words taken as written

indicators.note: the word you is said, giving the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone tells a worker they have finished a huge task and are a treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Bijou describes something small and elegant, a little jewel, so a gem is a fair noun sense.

clue.text: Narcotism, in altered state, for such as Coleridge

indicators.note: letters in an altered state have been rearranged, fitting a drug-induced surface

explanation.surface: A poet under the influence of opium, in a drug-altered state.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge famously wrote Kubla Khan under opium, so the narcotic surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was a leading English poet of the Romantic movement, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Votes for unknown characters from central Russia

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns
the middle of Russia holds two copies of the letter S, each spelt out as ess

explanation.surface: Ballots in favour of anonymous people from the heart of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour are ayes, also called yeses, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Hog a lot of time as 23

parts.note: a hog is a pig
an eon is an immensely long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone takes up far too much time, behaving like the person in another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The 23 entry is a homing bird, the kind that finds its way back to its loft, so this bird is that kind.

clue.text: Film star getting short romantic missive with love

indicators.note: the card word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a valentine is a love note sent on 14 February
love is nil in tennis scoring, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A movie idol receives a brief love letter with affection attached.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph Valentino was the silent-film heart-throb of the 1920s, so he is an example of a film star.

clue.text: Royalty for author

definitions.meaning: several English and Scottish kings bore this name, so it can stand for royalty
Joyce's first name was also this

explanation.surface: A payment made to a writer for their book sales.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'royalty' as the fee a writer earns; in fact it is a king's name, also the name of a novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Kings bearing the name stand for royalty, and novelist Henry James stands for an author.

clue.text: Female caught between happiness and ecstasy

indicators.note: the letter for caught sits between the two other pieces

parts.note: joy is a synonym of happiness
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A woman is trapped between delight and rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Joyce is a woman's given name, so a female is a loose definition by example.

clue.text: Without question, one clue needs revising — key is good use of language

indicators.note: a clue that needs revising must have its letters rewritten in a new order

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A setter admits one clue needs reworking, unquestioned, because fine language is what matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is read as 'with out': Q goes in with ONE CLUE and the mix is revised; E, a key, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloquence is fluent, persuasive speaking or writing, which is exactly a good use of language.

clue.text: See 19
Run into my position in field with small force Achilles led

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
mid-on is a fielding position in cricket, near the bowler on the leg side
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels

explanation.surface: A cricketer runs to their place in the field with a little band of men led by a Greek hero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Myrmidons were the warriors Achilles led at Troy in Homer's Iliad, so they were his force.

clue.text: Zero return after call for capital

indicators.note: the turned zero follows the naming word

parts.note: to dub is to call or name

indicators.note: the word for zero comes back, read from its end

parts.note: nil means zero

explanation.surface: A scoreless comeback follows a summons to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dublin is the capital city of Ireland, a definition by example; the city is the setting of Joyce's novel.

clue.text: Bush, as graduate, really confused about university

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about the university letter
the letters of really are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: President Bush, as a graduate, is truly muddled about university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the president; it is a shrub. 'confused' rearranges REALLY into YLAREL, and 'about' puts it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: The bay laurel is an evergreen shrub whose leaves are used in cooking, so it is an example of a bush.

clue.text: Heartless war and the like, hard for unfortunate person

indicators.note: the word war loses its middle letter, its heart, leaving its ends

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and the like
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Cruel warfare and similar hardships make for a pitiable victim.
explanation.definitionFit: A wretch is a miserable, unhappy person, so an unfortunate person is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Account of events showing husband is right

parts.note: a Tory is a right-winger, a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A record showing that a husband is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: History is a narrative of past happenings, so an account of events is a direct sense.

clue.text: President initially not differing from United States government

definitions.text: President initially not differing from United States government

parts.words: President initially not differing from United States government
parts.note: the eighteenth US president's three initials are the same as the initials of United States Government

explanation.surface: A new president who changes nothing in how America is run.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-word name splits over three lights; the first word is also the title of Joyce's novel, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Civil War general became the eighteenth president, and his initials U, S, G match the government's.

clue.text: Irish quarter in turmoil as result

indicators.note: letters in turmoil are thrown into confusion and rearranged

explanation.surface: A part of Ireland thrown into disorder as a consequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Troubles' surface fits: Ulster was in turmoil for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, so it is a quarter of the island.

clue.text: King who has feast after Christmas?

definitions.meaning: a king of England in the twelfth century bore this name
the first Christian martyr's saint's day is 26 December, the day after Christmas

explanation.surface: A monarch who carries on feasting once Christmas is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Good King Wenceslas looked out 'on the Feast of Stephen', which nudges toward a king. Stephen Dedalus is also a Joyce hero.
explanation.definitionFit: King Stephen ruled England in the 1100s, and Saint Stephen's feast day falls on 26 December.

clue.text: Sailor's laconic moral statement

definitions.meaning: the seafaring hero of the Arabian Nights tales
read as two words it is a terse verdict that wrongdoing is wrong

explanation.surface: A seaman's terse comment on right and wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The voyager of the Arabian Nights is a sailor, and split in two the name tersely says wrongdoing is wicked.

clue.text: Flag that man's writing for ethnic idioms

parts.note: a flag is a kind of iris, the yellow water flower
his means belonging to that man
MS, manuscript, is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A banner bearing a man's handwriting shows phrases peculiar to one people.
explanation.definitionFit: Irishisms are expressions typical of English as spoken in Ireland, so they are idioms of an ethnic group.

clue.text: Animated 13's all-round achievement as striker

definitions.meaning: the cartoon father of the family named in 13
in baseball a batter, the striker, who hits a home run goes all the way round the bases

explanation.surface: A cartoon character's all-round success as an attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet who wrote the Odyssey, Ulysses' story, gives the name too, though no clue words point to him. A 'homer' is a home run in baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon father in the 13 family bears this name, and a home run takes the batter round all the bases.

clue.text: Perspective provided by early European immigrant

definitions.meaning: a particular point of view on a story, as in a fresh take
the ... were a Germanic people who settled in Britain in the fifth century

explanation.surface: A viewpoint offered by one of the first settlers from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter's take on a story is its slant, and one of the early Germanic settlers of England was one of the Angles.

clue.text: See 19 across
Flower's sudden growth around lake

indicators.note: the growth word goes round the lake letter

parts.note: a boom is a sudden surge of growth, as in trade
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A plant's spurt of growth beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Leopold Bloom is the hero of Joyce's novel, celebrated on Bloomsday.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloom is a flower, especially one on an ornamental plant: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Concerning resistance to a head, try to be too clever

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
R is the physics symbol for resistance
each means per person, so a head

explanation.surface: Talk of opposition to a leader, someone tries something too smart.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreach is to fail by attempting too much, so trying to be too clever is a fair idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Ruin of the French city of Paris

parts.note: des is French for of the, in the plural
Paris was the Trojan prince, so his city was Troy

explanation.surface: Destruction of a French capital, Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the French capital, but it is the prince of Troy who carried off Helen.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck it entirely, so the verbs are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Part of press immersed in scoop — late news

indicators.note: the letters lie submerged across the words that follow, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: A journalist is buried in an exclusive story of breaking news.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'press' looks like newspapers, but it is a printing press.
explanation.definitionFit: A platen is the plate in a printing press that pushes the paper against the type, so it is part of one.
